families.s: HSE quarry design and health-and-safety-document guidance
families.t: quarry layout, faces, roads, tips, lagoons, plant selection, public risk, vehicle rules, shotfiring rules and document review
f: A quarry should be designed, managed and maintained to protect workers and the public.
Design should address face heights, plant layout, roads, tips, lagoons and extraction methods.
Roads should be suitable for the largest vehicles and expected traffic movements.
Geotechnical conditions can restrict face design and blasting methods.
The health and safety document records how significant quarry risks are controlled.
The document should include relevant excavation, tip, vehicle and shotfiring rules.
Plant selection and traffic arrangements should follow the designed operating system.
The design and document should be reviewed when geology, equipment, extraction or site conditions change.
families.g: Quarry design risk depends on geology, faces and tips, water and lagoons, road geometry, plant and traffic, blasting, public proximity, documented rules and change review.

families.s: HSE quarry tips, excavations, faces and inspection guidance
families.t: tip construction, stable ground, cross gradient, edge protection, excavation faces, overhangs, geotechnical assessment, inspection and remedial action
f: Quarry tips and excavations can fail and cause vehicle, engulfment or ground-movement incidents.
Tips should be constructed using an appropriate method and stable foundation.
Vehicles should tip on stable ground without unsafe cross gradient.
Tipping should occur at controlled positions with suitable edge protection and operating rules.
Faces should be designed and worked to prevent dangerous overhangs and falls of material.
Geotechnical conditions should be assessed by competent people where significant hazards exist.
Tips, excavations and supporting controls require suitable inspection and records.
Unsafe areas should be isolated and remedial work planned before normal operations resume.
families.g: Tip and excavation risk depends on geology and material, height and slope, water, foundation, vehicle position, edge protection, face condition, inspection, weather and operating method.

families.s: HSE quarry vehicle, haul-road, edge-protection and tipping guidance
families.t: haul roads, vehicle visibility, seat belts, edge protection, gradients, tipping, traffic separation, maintenance and driver competence
f: Quarry haul roads begin at the site entrance and should be designed for the vehicles using them.
Inadequate edge protection is a frequent cause of serious quarry vehicle risk.
Road edges, tips and water hazards need barriers or bunds suited to the largest vehicle.
Road surfaces, drainage, width, gradients and bends should allow controlled travel.
Visibility around earthmoving vehicles and separation from pedestrians should be managed.
Seat restraints should be used where provided and required.
Tipping should occur only at authorised stable locations under a defined procedure.
Vehicle checks, maintenance, driver competence, speed and supervision should match the quarry environment.
families.g: Quarry vehicle risk depends on road and edge design, gradients and surfaces, vehicle size and visibility, pedestrian separation, tipping position, restraints, maintenance, competence and weather.

families.s: HSE ports workplace-transport, lifting and freight-container safety guidance
families.t: vehicles, pedestrians, ship-shore interfaces, cranes, lifting accessories, containers, twistlocks, suspended loads, inspection and communication
f: Ports combine workplace vehicles, pedestrians, ships, cranes and cargo-handling equipment in constrained areas.
Traffic routes and operating zones should separate pedestrians from vehicles and mobile plant.
Loading, unloading, trailer coupling and ship access require planned controls.
Port lifting operations use cranes and accessories that require competent planning, inspection and operation.
Containers should be released from securing systems before lifting and incompatible or damaged fittings controlled.
Suspended loads and crane operating envelopes should be kept clear of unnecessary people.
Freight containers and lifting points should be checked for damage and suitability.
Drivers, crane operators, banksmen and ship or shore teams need clear communication and agreed signals.
families.g: Port transport and lifting risk depends on traffic and ship layout, cargo and container condition, cranes and accessories, securing systems, pedestrians, visibility, communication, weather and competence.

families.s: HSE fairground organiser, ride-controller and annual-inspection guidance
families.t: site layout, emergency plan, ride interaction, trained staff, crowd control, daily checks, maintenance, annual inspection, restraints and public safety
f: Fair organisers should plan, manage and monitor the site for worker and public safety.
Ride layout should prevent unsafe interaction and provide safe public access and exit.
Emergency plans should cover fire, overcrowding, ride collapse and severe weather.
Emergency routes, assembly areas, communication and trained responsible people should be provided.
Daily checks should cover access, firefighting equipment, closed areas, ground and housekeeping.
Ride controllers are responsible for safe erection, operation, maintenance and dismantling of their devices.
Fairground rides require annual inspection by a competent person and should not operate with an expired test.
Restraints, height or capability limits and safety instructions should be applied to protect riders.
families.g: Fairground risk depends on ride design and condition, layout and interaction, setup and dismantling, operators, inspection and maintenance, restraints, crowds, weather, emergency routes and public behaviour.
